ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure is the circuit diagram of a DC motor used for lifting heavy objects during operation. The internal resistance of the motor is $r = 1\Omega$, another resistor in the circuit is $R = 10\Omega$, the DC voltage is $U = 150V$, and the reading of the ideal voltmeter is $U_V = 120V$.

1. What is the current through the electric motor?
2. What is the electrical power input to the motor?
3. What is the output power of the electric motor?
4. If the motor lifts the object vertically upward at a constant speed of $v = 1\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$, find the mass of the object. (Take $g = 10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^2$)

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure is the circuit diagram of a DC motor used for lifting heavy objects during operation. The internal resistance of the motor is $r = 1\Omega$, another resistor in the circuit is $R = 10\Omega$, the DC voltage is $U = 150V$, and the reading of the ideal voltmeter is $U_V = 120V$. 1. What is the current through the electric motor? 2. What is the electrical power input to the motor? 3. What is the output power of the electric motor? 4. If the motor lifts the object vertically upward at a constant speed of $v = 1\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$, find the mass of the object. (Take $g = 10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^2$)
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a DC power supply, labeled with voltage U; at the upper right of the circuit there is a resistor R; below the resistor is connected a motor symbol M; across the two ends of the motor is connected in parallel an ideal voltmeter V. Therefore the circuit can be regarded as the resistor R and the motor connected in series, with the voltmeter connected in parallel across the two ends of the motor and not shunting current. Reasoning: The reading of the ideal voltmeter is the motor terminal voltage, U_V = 120 V. The total voltage of the power supply U = 150 V, so the voltage on the series resistor R is U_R = U - U_V = 150 - 120 = 30 V. Since R = 10 Ω, the series current is also the current through the motor: I = U_R / R = 30 / 10 = 3 A. The input electric power of the motor is P_in = U_V I = 120 × 3 = 360 W. The internal resistance of the motor r = 1 Ω, and the copper loss power is P_loss = I^2 r = 3^2 × 1 = 9 W. The output mechanical power of the motor is P_out = P_in - P_loss = 360 - 9 = 351 W. When lifting vertically at uniform speed, the mechanical output power P_out = mgv, therefore m = P_out / (gv) = 351 / (10 × 1) = 35.1 kg.
